Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

destroy verb

also destruction, wipe out, ruin, wreck, overthrow, be destroyed, do someone in, do in, he has done me in, finish off, raze to the ground, level

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: sī Juppiter saepe urbēs dēlēvit, frūgēs perdidit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cat. 4.21: Carthāginem

dēleō, dēlēre, dēlēvī, dēlētum

verb, second conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

destroy, wipe out

To wipe out completely: a city, an army, a name, a memory. Its first sense is to blot out writing, to erase (Cic. Clu. 41).

Other words

  • ēvertō, ēvertere, ēvertī, ēversum — overturn, overthrow

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1, 24 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Amic. 23 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Properly to turn upside down, upset (a boat, Cic. de Or. 1.174); then to overthrow a city, a house, a state, a fortune.

  • perdō, perdere, perdidī, perditum — ruin, destroy; lose, waste

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 131 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 315 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To make away with: ruin a person, destroy crops. Its everyday sense is to lose or waste something (operam perdere, to waste one’s effort). Its passive is pereō.

  • pessum dare — ruin, do someone in

    also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 2.6.23: pessum dedistī mē blandimentīs tuīs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 305

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut.; Cic. in fragmentīs)

Examples

  • quae enim domus tam stabilis, quae tam firma cīvitās est, quae nōn odiīs et discidiīs funditus possit ēvertī?

    for what house is so stable, what state so firm, that hatred and quarrels could not overturn it from the ground up?Cic. Amic. 23

  • Perdidit mē.

    He has done me in.Traupman 305

  • solō aequāre

    to raze to the groundTraupman 369

  • solō aequāta omnia

    everything was levelled to the groundLiv. 24.47 (Lewis & Short s.v. solum)

See also demolish, damage, break, ruins, burn.
